title: Resume a VCF Operations alert sweep across access-token expiry
prompt:
Fix access-token expiry handling and request encoding in the `vcfops_alerts` package under src/. It is a dependency-free, standard-library-only Python client for the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 API -- the `/suite-api` API served by VCF Operations itself, not the separate log management API. Running `python3 -m vcfops_alerts` acquires an access token, sweeps alerts and writes a JSON report.

Two things are wrong.

First, the token issued by acquireToken expires part way through a sweep, and the client throws away everything it has collected when that happens. Today a 401 unwinds the entire sweep, a replacement token is acquired, and the sweep starts over from page 0, re-fetching pages and alert details it had already retrieved. Instead the client must acquire a replacement token and put the interrupted request back on the wire once, so the sweep keeps its place: across a whole run each page and each alert detail must be fetched successfully exactly once, however many times the token dies, and everything collected before an expiry must survive it. Re-authenticate only in response to a 401 -- the `validity` the server advertises is far in the future and must not be second-guessed by refreshing pre-emptively or on a timer. Attempt at most one refresh per request, so a credential that is genuinely unusable surfaces as `TokenExpired` instead of looping. Every request issued after a refresh must carry the new token.

Second, both request bodies are built by filling in every property the schema allows. `authSource` in `username-password` is optional, and every property of `alert-query` is optional. A field the caller did not set must be absent from the JSON body rather than sent as `null`, `""` or `[]`: with no filters at all the alert-query body is `{}`, and with no `--auth-source` given the acquire body carries only `username` and `password`. A value the caller did set is sent as given, including a literal `false`.

Keep the rest of the behaviour as it is:

- Public API: `VcfOperationsClient(base_url, username, password, auth_source=None, ...)` with `acquire_token()`, `query_alerts(page, page_size, filters=None)`, `get_alert(alert_id)` and a `token_acquisitions` count; `sweep_alerts(client, page_size, filters=None, detail_levels=...)` returning a `SweepResult` whose `as_report(client)` keys stay as they are; and the existing `python3 -m vcfops_alerts` flags.
- Sweep order: walk pages upward from 0, sending `page` and `pageSize` explicitly on every queryAlert call rather than relying on the spec defaults, until the accumulated count reaches the reported `pageInfo.totalCount` or a page comes back empty. Then fetch details with getAlert for each collected alert whose `alertLevel` is one of the requested detail levels, in the order the alerts were returned, once per alert id.
- Wire details: acquireToken is unauthenticated and must not carry an Authorization header; authenticated calls send the `Authorization` value format pinned in the contract; POST bodies go out as `application/json`; getAlert sends no body and no query string.

docs/contract.json is the local source of truth for paths, methods, parameter names, body properties and the Authorization value format. It is derived from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository at the commit recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Use only the three operations it names: acquireToken, queryAlert and getAlert.

Standard library only -- no third-party packages. Do not edit docs/contract.json, docs/official_sources.json, tests/mock_vcfops.py or tests/verify.py.

tests/mock_vcfops.py is a loopback mock of exactly those three operations that records every request it receives. tests/verify.py starts it, runs the CLI against it twice with different credentials and filters, and judges the recorded requests. Check your work with `python3 tests/verify.py`.
